standard.title: First Nations dance
standard.description: explore examples of dance choreographed and/or performed by First Nations Australians
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how the arts are important for communities at Foundation, including listening to First Nations Australians talk about arts and connection to Country/Place. They can observe and describe dance features (AC9ADA2E01).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore examples of dance choreographed and/or performed by First Nations Australians.

nodes.label: When and why First Nations Australians dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify when and why First Nations Australians use dance — including connections to significant occasions, ceremonies and community events.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least one occasion when First Nations Australians use dance (e.g. NAIDOC Week, ceremonies) and a reason why.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring when, where, how and why First Nations Australians use dance to share cultural knowledge — including celebrations such as NAIDOC Week, National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children's Day, Reconciliation Week, Sorry Day; identifying dance in First Nations cultural expressions at school, in community, and in state/national events.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians use dance in specific significant events — noticing how performers and audiences observe protocols and respect Elders and knowledge holders

Explore First Nations Australians' interpretations of the night sky — working with community members who have cultural authority to co-create movements representing shapes and patterns visible at different times of year

response_modes.reason: Understanding the range of occasions and purposes requires exposure to multiple examples — single-example exposure risks tokenism. Use resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who encounter multiple contexts in which First Nations Australians use dance develop genuine understanding of dance as living cultural practice — not a historical artefact. This foundation supports respectful engagement with First Nations content throughout F-10.
success_criteria: Student can name at least one occasion when First Nations Australians use dance
Student can explain one reason why dance is important in that context

nodes.label: Observing elements in First Nations dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe how elements of dance are used in choreography and/or performance by First Nations Australians.
nodes.minimum_width: Observing one example of First Nations Australian dance and describing at least one element of dance used (e.g. movement type, level, relationship).
nodes.typical_width: Observing examples of First Nations Australian dance using learnt element vocabulary; noticing how movements, relationships, space and time are used; exploring movements with representatives of the First Nations Australian community or via resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians.
wider: Co-create movements with a First Nations Australian community member who has cultural authority — exploring how specific movements represent cultural knowledge
Compare element use in two examples of First Nations Australian dance from different communities or occasions
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot yet apply element observation to First Nations dance will engage only at a surface cultural level — missing the connection between element choices and cultural meaning that underpins respectful engagement in later bands.

response_modes.reason: Apply the same Viewpoints questions used in E01 — 'What movements do you see?', 'What levels?', 'What relationships between dancers?' — to First Nations dance examples. Familiarity with the observational frame transfers across contexts.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one element of dance used in a First Nations Australian dance example
Student engages with First Nations dance examples with respect and attentiveness
